  > What I checked and found supported: the headline numbers (closure, k* with CIs/censoring, greedy-vs-random gaps, paired shift comparisons, theory gaps) all match `results/*.csv`; deviations are reported as they fell; negative results (H1, H2 margin, H4, coherence, vacuous Chernoff) are stated.
  > 
  > **must M1 — the setting with missing cells is never evaluated.** The objective's setting is a leaderboard matrix with missing cells and a new model with k measured entries. Every result is on dense blocks cut from the leaderboard (124 of 535 models x 70 of 567 tasks; 117 x 247 of 535 x 1256) which, by Table 1, differ systematically from the rest (outside models larger, newer, 0.7-0.9 SD higher). A masked-EM factor model exists in `code/bmk/fa.py` but is not run on a sparse matrix; the history sweep masks cells of the history only, test models stay complete. Narrowing the claim to "the pool" is honest but does not answer whether greedy selection + factor model works on the matrix as it is.
  > Answer with: the grouped protocol on the full sparse MTEB matrix, or graded-density subsets (coverage e.g. >=30/50/70%), factor model by masked EM, candidate set = benchmarks observed for the test model, targets = random 30% of its observed cells; greedy A vs random vs column mean, k-curve with family-clustered intervals, and a stated LOBO analogue for closure. A main-text paragraph/figure plus an appendix table suffices; the dense-pool results stay as the controlled experiment. Owners: experiment-repo (run), figtab-repo (figure/table), paper-repo (text).
  > 
  > may: (m1) abstract: say the pre-specified 10% margin of H2 is met on one pool of three; (m2) checklist: "seven limitations" vs six in Section 7, "5-20 CPU minutes" vs 2-22 in Appendix D; (m3) define "closure" and "A-optimal" in a clause in the abstract; (m4) say where the pre-specification is recorded (Brief revision/commit).
